% ---------------- ABSTRACT ----------------
\chapter*{ABSTRACT}

Large language models are increasingly executed on personal machines,
where they can invoke tools that read files, run shell commands and
access the web, yet users have little visibility into or control over
these actions. Orb addresses this gap as a governance-first command
console for local and cloud language models. The system places a
governed Express/TypeScript gateway between the user and the model: it
routes chat requests either to local Ollama models or to cloud
providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Groq, Mistral), enforces a per-tool
execution policy of automatic, policy-based or manual approval,
streams responses to a Next.js frontend, and persists sessions, audit
logs, provider connector keys and extracted memory facts in SQLite.
Every programmatic request through the Bearer-token API is fully
audited with request messages, tool calls, policy decisions, latency
and token counts. An asynchronous post-chat analysis stage extracts
durable user facts into a per-user memory store and computes a
hallucination-risk score for each response. Authentication is handled
by Clerk for interactive users and by hashed API keys for external
clients. The result is a working oversight layer that demonstrates how
policy enforcement, auditability and telemetry can be added around
both local and cloud model inference without modifying the models
themselves.

This report documents the background, system analysis, requirement
specification and design of Orb in its current state. It covers the
existing-system landscape and its limitations, the proposed system and
its features, the functional and non-functional requirements, the
system architecture, data flow and database design, the interface
design of the console, and the implementation, testing and results of
the working system, followed by the conclusion, future enhancements,
user manual and project planning.
